items.content: TAXONOMY RULING (operator reh3376, 2026-08-13): A policy document (SECURITY.md, docs/features/*.md), a sprint post-mortem, or any node whose primary content is DESCRIPTIVE of a rule rather than a directly-invokable rule statement MUST NOT classify as an APPLICABLE must-constraint in consulting.classify. The underlying rule the doc DESCRIBES may still be a separate must-constraint node in its own right; this ruling targets the doc-node classification specifically. Correct classification for policy-doc / post-mortem / SECURITY.md nodes is none (not applicable to current action). Affects consulting.classify + downstream Jiminy surfacing. Resolves surface-items pass1/#2 (SECURITY.md) + pass2/#2 (EXPORT-SCRUB-INTAKE-001 post-mortem) + a recurring class in JIMINY-CORPUS.

ARCHITECTURAL DIRECTIVE 2026-08-01 (operator): Jimini's purpose is to ENFORCE hard constraints on the main LLM's behavior, not merely advise. When the main LLM violates a Jiminy constraint, the user MUST be alerted. Jiminy's overarching purpose is to force the stateless + probabilistic nature of an LLM into a stateful + deterministic set of behaviors. The enforcement cycle MUST be RSIC-governed so Jiminy continuously learns from its own enforcement decisions (false-blocks weaken the constraint; missed-violations strengthen or extend coverage). The current default-advisory + opt-in /strict architecture is MISALIGNED with this intent — /strict should be the DEFAULT, coverage MUST extend beyond Write/Edit to include Bash (and any other action-producing tool), and violations MUST both block AND alert. This directive supersedes any prior framing of Jiminy as advisory-by-design.

J17 trust score 25.4% (and Jiminy actionable compliance ~14% steady state) are NOT harmless-by-design. Operator (2026-08-01): trust reflects the receiving agents confidence in MDEMG guidance; 25.4% means the agent has learned to distrust because most surfaced items are not worth acting on. Reframe: the ~14% honest steady state and the 25.4% trust EMA are the same substrate-quality signal seen from producer + receiver sides. Do not normalize either as acceptable. The JIMINY-CORPUS + HITL-CURATION + Lever-C-tuning arc must actually raise follow rate + trust, not just make the dashboards render the low number in green.
Do NOT use glob/grep to search for file paths. Instead, query MDEMG CMS to discover file paths and code structure.
Markdown memory files (.claude/memory/) are REMINDERS AND KEYS only — not actual memory. All real persistent memory lives in MDEMG CMS (Neo4j graph in mdemg-dev space).

CORRECTION: Sprint plans (and all project planning docs) belong in docs/development/<sprint-line>/ inside the repo — NOT in ~/Downloads/. The mdemg repo has an established pattern at docs/development/ft-lora/ for the local-LoRA sprint line; mirror it with docs/development/ft-oai/ for the OpenAI FT sprint line. Reason: Downloads is ephemeral user space — docs there are not versioned with the code, not discoverable via repo grep, not visible to reviewers on a PR. This applies to sprint plans, design docs, decision memos — anything that informs or documents work on the repo. When drafting a new planning doc, check for an existing docs/development/<topic>/ directory first; create one to match the existing ft-lora pattern if the sprint line is new.

When creating a JSON schema, contract, or test spec that will be used repeatedly, you MUST use the established UxTS framework family rather than ad-hoc JSON: UATS for HTTP API contract tests (docs/api/api-spec/uats/specs/), UITS for UI/cross-component flow specs (docs/tests/uits/specs/), UOBS for observability/metrics, ULTS for LLM prompt contracts, etc. Adding/changing an API response field (e.g. status on /v1/backup/list) MUST update the corresponding UATS spec; UI tab assertions belong in the UITS framework + Playwright, not ad-hoc. The 15 UxTS frameworks are catalogued in docs/tests/UXTS_FRAMEWORK_MATRIX.md and CI-gated via the drift checker.
CORRECTION REINFORCEMENT: never trust an unordered sample for novelty — the earlier assumption was wrong and must not recur. Use exact nearest-neighbor ranking.

REQUIREMENT (formalized 2026-05-01 by reh3376): Live system testing is a required testing tier for every sprint that touches code paths exercised in production. Mocked unit + integration tests are necessary but not sufficient. Tier 3 E2E means: the real binary running against the real services it depends on, with real outputs observed via TSDB queries / Grafana panels / log inspection — not mocked clients. Evidence basis: across Phase 11.6.x, 11.6.2, and 12.0-12.6, every major defect was caught in live smoke runs while unit/integration tests passed. Six cutover-bypass sites, five latent UVTS-runner defects, the host.docker.internal DNS issue, the panel-3 SQL false-positive — all surfaced only when running the live system. Sprint plans must include a verification-checklist item of the form: live smoke: run X against the real system, observe Y in TSDB/Grafana/logs, confirm Z. Surprise bugs caught during live smoke get their own follow-up fix-commit; do not silently roll them into the sprint commit. The live system can be the operator local stack (mdemg native binary + Docker Compose) — the point is real I/O on the real wire, not production scale.

RECURRING BUG (3rd occurrence): OpenAI chat/completions API — newer models (gpt-5.x, gpt-4.1+) REQUIRE the `max_completion_tokens` parameter; `max_tokens` is rejected with HTTP 400 `Unsupported parameter` error. ALL new LLM-calling code that targets OpenAI must use `max_completion_tokens`. MLX-local and legacy OpenAI-compatible endpoints still accept `max_tokens`. Pattern: `token_key = "max_completion_tokens" if "api.openai.com" in base_url else "max_tokens"`. Discovered again 2026-04-22 in `neural/training/distill_driver.py` — patched in _chat_completion(). Check codebase proactively when writing any new OpenAI HTTP wrapper.

RULE: ALWAYS add a detailed sprint summary as a PR comment every time a new PR is created, including auto-created PRs from pushing to a dev branch. Auto-created PRs have no body by default, so the comment is the only structured record. Summary must cover: sprint ID/title, epics completed, commits per epic (with short hashes), findings/issues addressed, key metrics (test results, empirical data), live integration test results, and verification gates (build/lint/test). Detect the PR via gh pr list --state open after push, then gh pr comment <num> --body-file -. This is proactive — part of done for every PR.

CONSTRAINT: Never modify production database schemas without a migration file. Always use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and index creation with IF NOT EXISTS guards. Direct ALTER TABLE on production is forbidden.

All sprint development plans MUST follow the standardized 12-section format (v1.0). Required sections: Header & Metadata, Problem Statement, Scope & Constraints, Dependencies & Pre-Conditions, Implementation Plan (sequential epics with gates), Testing Plan (3 tiers: unit + integration + e2e — never skip), Commit Strategy, Verification Checklist, Documentation Update (final epic — never cut for time), Risks & Mitigations, Documents Accessed. Optional: Rollback Procedures (for destructive ops). Recall format via: POST /v1/skills/sprint-planning/recall or filter_tags skill:sprint-planning
You must never use UUID v4 in this codebase. Always use CUIDv2.

We cannot make good decisions and properly optimize the effectiveness of the MDEMG framework if we do not have reliable and consistent data to base our decisions on and drive our algorithms. The correctness and consistency of this data capture is the absolute core base infrastructure — without it the goals and vision of MDEMG can never be achieved. We MUST master these data pipelines and their historical collection.

CRITICAL CORRECTION: Do NOT modify code without first switching to planning mode and creating a development plan. This codebase is too complex for on-the-fly changes without context research. The goreleaser nfpm fix (removing type:glob, adding submodules:recursive) was made as a reactive hotfix without planning — exactly the behavior being constrained. Must enter plan mode BEFORE any code modification, research context, then propose changes. Jiminy should detect and redirect when code modifications are attempted without an active plan.

After completing development of new features/functionality that requires rebuild and restart of mdemg server, it should occur automatically without requiring user input. Build + restart should be part of the development completion flow.

[must] All unique identifiers in MDEMG must use CUIDv2 (nrednav/cuid2), NOT UUID v4. This is a project-scoped requirement across main repo and all submodules. CUIDv2 is collision-resistant, k-sortable, and shorter. uuid.New() and uuid.NewString() are banned patterns. Use cuid2.Generate() instead.

After merging a PR to main via --admin, if the dev branch has more work to push, rebase the dev branch onto main (git pull --rebase origin main) BEFORE pushing the next commit. This keeps the branch linear and avoids merge commits that force squash-merging. In PR #172, the GPG fix was admin-merged to main via PR #171, then the docs commit was pushed to reh3376_dev01 without rebasing — git created a merge commit, resulting in 4 commits (3 real + 1 merge) that required squash to keep history clean.

MANDATORY RULE: Never leave discovered issues unresolved. When issues are found during development — even if unrelated to the current task — they must be either (1) fixed immediately, or (2) documented and tracked for resolution once the current task set completes. Suggesting to skip, ignore, or defer issues indefinitely is NEVER acceptable. At minimum, note the issue explicitly and return to it. This applies to test failures, bugs, lint warnings, stale data, broken endpoints, missing checks — everything. Jiminy should monitor for and correct any agent behavior that suggests skipping discovered issues.

Every sprint that touches a pipeline must include an end-to-end verification step against live data, not just go test ./.... Unit tests alone are insufficient — must verify actual observable output from the running system.

FEEDBACK: When troubleshooting, never stop at the first break found. Trace the ENTIRE pipeline end-to-end and document ALL breaks before proposing a fix. This prevents recurring pseudo-fixes that only address one break while leaving others intact. The J17 protocol issue is a case study: multiple previous fixes each addressed one break but the system remained broken because other breaks existed downstream.

CRITICAL PROCESS: When fixing a pipeline, a fix is NOT done when the code compiles or tests pass. It is done when the actual end-to-end observable output (dashboard metric, API response, log line) shows the correct value. Each fix must be followed by running the pipeline and verifying the output. If the output is still wrong, trace why and fix the next break. This is iterative — do not declare victory until the metric reads correctly. The J17 protocol fix required 12 breaks across 5 iterations of run-trace-fix cycles, not just the initial 7 identified statically.

USER PREFERENCE: When planning complex features or fixes, ALWAYS use the most advanced coding model available (Opus). Never delegate planning or architecture to Haiku. Haiku is only for simple mechanical tasks: file searches, grep, status checks. Sub-agent model selection: Haiku=simple/fast, Sonnet=medium analysis, Opus=planning/architecture/complex fixes.

MANDATORY PROCESS: After a new feature is created in the development plan, a documentation file MUST be created that explains the new functionality and provides links to relevant documentation. IF new APIs or UATS specs are involved, docs/development/API_REFERENCE.md MUST also be updated. This applies to ALL future phases.

CONSTRAINT: NEVER commit directly to main branch. All development work happens on mdemg-dev01. Main is branch-protected — changes reach it only via PR. The auto-pr.yml workflow creates PRs automatically on push to mdemg-dev01. Always verify branch before any git operation: git branch --show-current must show mdemg-dev01.

MANDATORY: Every phase development doc MUST end with a Documents Accessed list — every file read or referenced during development. This list is the definitive source for which docs need updating before commit. Without it, docs like README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, API_REFERENCE.md get missed. The user calls these all relevant documentation.

Mandatory workflow rule: Linting must be checked and pass before changes can be committed. Add golangci-lint run to the verification sequence: implement → lint → e2e test → update docs → stage → commit.

CMS Memory Protection Constraint: (1) Trigger Neo4j backup of mdemg-dev space when no active codebase operations are in progress. (2) Check CMS health via /healthz during sessions; investigate anomalies immediately. (3) Record critical observations (corrections, key decisions) with high surprise scores to ensure persistence. (4) On DB failure, check backups/ directory, restore Neo4j, verify mdemg-dev space integrity.

CORRECTION: Never use git stash as a workaround for goreleaser dirty-state checks. The correct approach is to commit all pending changes BEFORE running goreleaser release. If files are not ready to commit, they should be properly handled (committed as WIP, or the release should wait). Stashing to bypass tool checks is a bad practice that leaves orphaned state.
MDEMG codebase ingestion must use space_id=mdemg-dev (Claude CMS space), NOT a separate space. This ensures codebase knowledge is co-located with conversation memory for recall.
NEVER use mdemg db start — ALWAYS use docker compose up -d neo4j. The mdemg db start command creates a DIFFERENT volume with EMPTY data.

CORRECTION: Never hardcode values in production code. Always use configurable variables (CLI flags, env vars, config files). Hardcoded values create static code that requires source modification to change behavior — users should be able to configure runtime behavior without understanding or modifying the code. Use defaults as fallbacks, but expose every configurable value through the configuration hierarchy. Why: Hardcoded paths, endpoints, space IDs, timeouts, and model names make code non-portable, non-reusable, and require code changes for what should be operational configuration. This was caught in the benchmark runner which had hardcoded CODEBASE_PATH, MDEMG_ENDPOINT, MDEMG_SPACE_ID, etc.
User preference: Always create tables and charts in markdown files with mermaid diagrams, not ASCII art. This applies to all observations, documentation, and generated content.
Standing directive: If a test failure is found during any work, it is my responsibility to fix it immediately. Never leave a failure for someone else. Own every failure you encounter.

CORRECTION: Do NOT parallelize epics. Epic 1 (Foundation/Documentation) must complete fully before Epic 2 (Causal Insertion) begins. The documentation in Epic 1 drives the implementation in Epic 2. Running them concurrently short-circuits the design-first process.

[must] All development plans MUST include three testing tiers: unit tests, integration tests, AND e2e/live tests. Unit tests alone are insufficient — integration tests verify wiring between components, and e2e tests verify real behavior against running services. The neural sidecar metrics bug (latency=0, errors=0 when sidecar unreachable) was only caught by live testing, not unit tests. Plans must also include updating all relevant documentation as an explicit step. These are not optional extras — they are mandatory plan requirements.
